# Decisions: linked-context

- 2026-09-29T10:07:56.125Z — (superseded by D5) chose **No sub-initiative hierarchy. Records group and depend on each other through typed links at task grain (waits_on declared, cites derived); an umbrella is an initiative whose tasks link to its members.** over Parent/child sub-initiatives (beads-style parent-child edge) because Real dependencies are task→task/decision across records and a record often depends on several others; a tree allows one parent and says only 'belongs together', which a link already says. Phases already split work inside a record and supersession covers replacement. Proposed to the operator 2026-09-29; revisit if they rule otherwise.
- 2026-09-29T10:08:02.037Z — rule: **Never read the reach index or buildGraph from a hook, statusline or shim path for travel; read only the links tier.** — chose **Travel reads a write-time materialised hot tier, index-tier1 links/<slug>.json (neighbours pattern, cursor-incremental, target staleness by tail read), never the reach index or buildGraph** over Reading reach.json from SessionStart as the 2026-09-20 skeleton said, or folding neighbour logs at session start because The reach code is banned from hook bundles by graph-hotpath.test.ts (record-index 4.1) and record-graph D2 rejected N-log reads on the hot path; reach is refreshed only by sofar find and Rust has no reader. A narrow tier costs O(links) per read, predicted ≤0.5ms Rust.
- 2026-09-29T10:08:04.482Z — chose **Memory handles in the link grammar are qualified-only (<slug> M<n>); repo.md lines stay unnumbered and out of the graph** over Bare M<n> and minting repo.md line nodes, as the roadmap-h2 note 01M2ZDKDRACY87BA26VWN825VP proposed because repo-memory-capture D3 deferred memory nodes until a disambiguation rule exists and named qualified-only as the likely one; M<n> is per-initiative so a bare handle is ambiguous, and repo.md is hand-written with no ids (repo-memory-capture D1).
- 2026-09-29T10:08:07.307Z — chose **Readiness-gated travel: open waits_on targets and waits resolved since the block are asserted; derived cites are offered only in the remaining budget, focus-ranked with hub damping; zero bytes when nothing is open** over Rendering every linked target (all-links travel) or ranking by raw citation count or recency because record-index D2: declared relevance may be asserted, derived only offered. The common case costs 0 tokens and an open wait ~40-60; raw counts let hub records dominate (record-index D9). Graphiti/Letta/aider precedents: validity filter, fixed block budgets, damped ranking. Predictions and ablations in Phase 6.
- 2026-09-29T10:13:51.346Z — (supersedes D1) rule: **No sub initiatives — relate initiatives only through links.** — operator: "yes no sub initiatives" — chose **Operator ruling 2026-09-29: no sub-initiatives; D1's links-only design is confirmed** over Leaving D1 as an unratified proposal because The operator answered the D1 question directly
- 2026-09-29T10:28:13.447Z — chose **waits_on is stored as canonical qualified handles (lowercase slug + target; unqualified D/T/n.n qualified to home at write); absent leaves the set, present replaces, [] clears; a bare slug is a handle only in declared waits_on, never in scanned prose** over Storing handles as typed by the writer, append-only add/remove deltas, or letting prose bare slugs cite a record because The memory_promoted supersedes precedent stores qualified handles so a handle reads the same from any log; replace-on-present keeps the fold O(1) per event with no delta replay; SPEC already rules a bare slug in prose is not a citation, and scanning it would make every record-name mention an edge.
- 2026-09-29T10:28:13.447Z — chose **Resolution is per target and one hop: an unresolved task in a record closed done/dropped is resolved, in a superseded record moved (never followed into the successor); an initiative target follows its successor exactly one hop; decisions and memories never move** over Leaving tasks in closed records open forever, following supersession chains to the end, or resolving waits transitively because Closed done/dropped means no work remains coming from there (task-drop-state D1's RESOLVED sense); task ids are per-record so no successor task is the same task; one hop bounds each read to two logs and cannot loop on a supersession or waits_on cycle.
- 2026-09-29T11:09:07.857Z — chose **Travel block contract: seeds = focus task + blocked tasks, task-sourced links only, cross-record only; hub damping as 1/bit-length(in-degree) compared by integer cross-multiplication; YIELDING precedence 3 (after Memory and Repo memory, before decision index 3→4 and last session 4→5)** over Float 1/ln(in-degree) scores; travel claiming budget before memory (precedence 0) or as a PROTECTED block; seeding from decision/note/next-action cites; rendering home-record targets because Float logs are not guaranteed byte-identical across TS Math.log and Rust f64::ln (rust-core D1); integer bit length gives the same damping curve exactly. Dedupe must read what Repo memory actually rendered, so travel yields after it. Home targets already render in focus/phases/decision index. status.ts precedence comments (3, 4) renumber in Phase 5.
- 2026-09-29T11:18:43.107Z — chose **Travel goldens as ahead-of-code conformance cases (syn.travel-*, one home record per scenario in one synthetic fixture); a dangling line ends at `dangling` unless the handle's own target exists; a superseded initiative resolved via its successor renders the successor's status** over A separate travel suite with in-process rendering; skipped cases until 5.1; always or never labelling dangling lines because The SessionStart hook is the digest's black-box surface both TS and Rust already run; the `ahead` field keeps the cases green today (golden minus the block equals the reference byte for byte) and fails the day 5.1 matches whole, so the marker cannot be forgotten. Nothing binds a dangling handle so there is no label, but a superseded record with a missing successor still has a goal worth showing.
- 2026-09-29T14:13:47.706Z — chose **A full-replace plan_updated task that omits waits_on keeps the task's prior declared set, matched by id (first task wins); present replaces, [] clears** over Letting a full replace drop waits_on like every other task field it does not restate because SPEC §Links says absent leaves the set unchanged on plan task input too, and phase-lifecycle D8 forbids a full replace silently discarding data its caller did not restate. FP-18 pins it in both folds.
- 2026-09-29T14:30:13.987Z — chose **`sofar new --waits-on` seeds a plan (Phase 1, task 1.1 'Wait on <handles>') carrying the set, resolved before anything is created** over An initiative-level waits_on on initiative_created, or refusing --waits-on on a record with no tasks because SPEC Links puts declared links on tasks only and 2.1 shipped no initiative-level field; a seeded task is the umbrella shape SPEC names, needs no schema change, and a later plan replace keeps the set by id (D10).
- 2026-09-29T14:30:13.988Z — chose **Cycle warning uses beads readiness: edges task to task through OPEN targets only, a whole-initiative target stands for its open tasks, D/M have no out-edges, a write closing the task is not walked** over Warning any graph cycle including through done tasks, or following decisions' until tasks because A done/dropped task holds nothing back so a loop through it cannot deadlock; warning it would be noise the agent learns to ignore.
- 2026-09-29T14:47:30.619Z — chose **Reach cite sources: a next_action cite comes from the writing session's node (cli anchors none); a task's title and status-note cites come from task:<slug>#<id> (final plan only); one edge per (sourcing event, target); a title cite anchors at the event that last CHANGED the title text; task nodes stay out of an initiative seed's contents** over A new next-action node kind, one deduped edge per source node, anchoring title cites at every restating plan replace, or listing every task in contents because Session and task are existing node kinds, so no new vocabulary; per-event edges keep every cite checkable against the event holding the handle; a restating replace wrote nothing new; listing every task would flood initiative seeds, and 3.2 owns the surfaces
- 2026-09-29T14:58:59.442Z — chose **Graph cites mirror reach exactly: event_id+ts of the sourcing event on every cite edge, one edge per (sourcing event, target), title anchor via reach's exported titleKey; dangling stays on decision nodes only; related renders Cites/Cited-by only when non-empty; why unchanged** over Keeping graph cites as undeduped decision-only multi-edges without event ids, adding dangling[] to note/task nodes, or adding a cites block to why because A parity test can only prove one rule if both sides dedupe and anchor alike; no consumer reads dangling beyond decisions and the links tier (Phase 4) owns dangling for the new sources; a file is never a cite endpoint so why has nothing to show
- 2026-09-29T15:13:59.743Z — chose **Memory nodes are citation TARGETS only (memory:<event ulid>, occurrence family, ordinal = M<n>), with no session edge and not in an initiative seed's contents; a memory target obeys the decision no-future rule** over Adding a remembered session edge kind, listing memories in contents, making memory text a cite source, or letting a cite resolve a memory promoted after the sourcing event because SPEC Links names no memory source and no new occurrence edge; a target-only node needs no fold/adjacency change on the hot path. M ordinals are positional like D, so a handle written before the memory existed named nothing — the same reason decisions cannot be cited from the past.
- 2026-09-29T15:56:24.613Z — chose **Links tier = per-slug links/<slug>.json of TASK-sourced links only (waits_on + title/status-note cites), each with a target snapshot resolved from a links.json reducer that mirrors the fold (plan phases, statuses, declared sets, decision/memory supersession, record status). The file is trusted while the initiative set matches and every log it read holds; a grown log whose appended lines can't carry a link event revalidates by tail scan. Refreshed after every projected MCP append and at session start, in TS and Rust.** over Materialising decision/note/next-action cites too; building target snapshots by folding target logs with the real fold; keying the file on graph/tier stats plus recordQuiet over every log as neighbours does because SPEC's Travel block reads task-sourced links only, so the rest would be hot-path bytes nobody reads (4.2 can add them for in-degree). Folding target logs is the N-log read record-graph D2 rejects. Keying on only the logs actually read keeps a warm read at O(deps) stats, and the tail scan keeps it warm across hook appends: Rust 0.26ms, down from 2.4ms. Parity is proven three ways: against a fold-driven from-logs reference over all 64 real logs, byte for byte TS↔Rust, and against the syn.travel goldens.
- 2026-09-29T15:56:28.252Z — chose **Anchors and `at`: a waits_on handle anchors at the event that put it INTO the set (a restating replace keeps it, like the title rule); a task cite anchors at its latest sourcing event, ordered by first occurrence; a task's `at` is the event that last changed its status value; moved = latest APPLIED task_status_changed after the anchor; dangling cites are kept (never offered); a task in a record closed done/dropped resolves with the record's status event.** over Re-anchoring every handle at each event that restates the set; anchoring cites at their first mention; counting plan_updated restatements as moves; dropping dangling cites as reach does because If a restatement re-anchored the handle, a wait that resolved before it would drop out of "resolved since the block", which is the one case D4 exists to show. A cite's latest mention is the conservative "since". SPEC §Links says a task moves only on task_status_changed. D14 gives the links tier ownership of dangling for the new sources.
- 2026-09-29T15:56:31.498Z — chose **passOverRecord/pass_over_record gain an optional raw-line prefilter (`lines`): a line failing it is never JSON-decoded, and the cursor line is found by decoding backwards. The pass writes the meta whenever a cursor moves. The links filter passes `"type"<ws>:<ws>"<link event|correction>"` and ANY line containing `\u`.** over Decoding every line then filtering by type (the `relevant` hook alone); a bare substring match without the escape rule because JSON.parse is most of a cold pass: TS 57 of 69ms over this repo's 27.6k lines, of which the links tier needs 2,058. JSON can spell the type key and value only literally or through \u escapes, so the filter cannot miss a link event, and a false positive costs only a decode. Rust cold fell from 64 to 28ms and TS from 87 to 62ms.
- 2026-09-29T15:56:34.917Z — chose **Ship 4.1 with the cold-start prediction recorded as MISSED: the links tier adds about 20% to a cold session-start (Rust 164→196ms, TS 296→360ms), against the ≤5% predicted. Warm met its prediction: Rust +0.08ms on a quiet record and +0.26ms after a hook append (≤0.5ms predicted); TS +0.09/+0.30ms on a 59ms start (D18 allows +10%).** over Putting the tier behind a flag, or skipping it on a cold start (which would leave travel empty) because r1-fixes D18 gates warm p50s, and a cold start happens once per clone or index wipe. What remains is each tier re-reading all 25MB of logs on a cold start (read+UTF-8 is about 10ms in Rust and 29ms in TS), and only a cold read shared across tiers removes it. Skipping the tier breaks record-index D1, which allows a slower answer but never a wrong one.
- 2026-09-29T16:28:44.586Z — chose **Links deps keyed by log content (cursor id at offset), no mtime; links-in.json rebuilt on the full path only, trusted while its read logs gained no link line; a correction forces the full path** over stat/mtime keyed deps and per-target re-folds on every read because git rewrites mtime (cross-initiative-conflicts D1); the writer's own refresh keeps the reverse index current, and a correction can revive a dropped cite that a re-snapshot cannot see

Revisit only if 6.1's read-paths gate shows the travel read over budget.
